source.title: SVGD: A Virtual Gradients Descent Method for Stochastic Optimization

record.tranche_reason: Compares stochastic optimizers on natural-label classification tasks and reports test error, bearing on V4 with a different optimizer, SVGD.
record.gate_note: The study reports test errors for RMSProp, Adam, SGD, and SVGD. It does not report training errors or test random-label memorization; those parts of the claim are not tested.
record.test_reason: The study directly compares Adam and RMSProp with SGD using held-out classification error, the method and measure relevant to V4. Its proposed SVGD optimizer is not needed for this comparison.
record.authors_conclusion: The record accurately paraphrases the authors' conclusion: SVGD converges relatively faster and achieves better test accuracy than SGD, RMSProp and Adam in their experiments. This is their conclusion about SVGD, rather than an explicit conclusion about adaptive optimizers' generalization disadvantage.
record.recipe_differences: Introduces SVGD and compares it with RMSProp, Adam, and SGD using model-specific learning rates selected through hundreds of experiments; weight decay is used. It does not test random-label memorization.
record.method_sensitivity: Test error differs across optimizer and model/dataset; the model-specific learning rates also differ.

fits_no_version.finding: SVGD achieves lower reported test error than the three comparator optimizers on all three architectures.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Stochastic Virtual Gradient Descent can improve held-out classification performance over SGD, RMSProp and Adam in these training settings.

record.problems: Only test errors are tabulated, so training performance and the train-test gap cannot be compared. Learning rates are summarized as optimal after hundreds of experiments, but the tuning procedure and search budget are not detailed. The MNIST table is followed by text referring to CIFAR-10, creating an internal inconsistency about the test set.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and its coexistence with natural-label generalization.
Width variation beyond zero training error.
Matched convolutional-versus-fully-connected comparisons and local connectivity.

Language benchmarks; relative training performance; broader hyperparameter tuning; decoupled weight decay; switching optimizers. Learning rates and schedules were selected through hundreds of experiments, but the search and selection protocol is unspecified.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its association with generalization gaps.

record.verdict_notes: All adaptive-versus-SGD point estimates have V4's predicted direction, but the margins are small. The missing training-error and broader-tuning comparisons are untested components, not grounds for scope limitations. No reported significance test justifies classifying these differences as absent.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label fitting and natural-label generalization coexistence.
Convolutional versus fully connected architecture comparison.
Language benchmarks; comparison under a clearly limited tuning budget; effects of broader tuning, decoupled weight decay, or switching optimizers; training performance relative to test performance.
Sharpness or other measured properties tracking generalization gap.

relationships.condition: MNIST MLP, 3.75 epochs, with optimizer-specific learning-rate schedules
relationships.reason: R1–R3 show only small penalties: RMSProp 1.80% and Adam 1.94% versus SGD 1.76%; no uncertainty establishes their reliability.
relationships.display_finding: Reported small error penalties for RMSProp and Adam relative to SGD remain unverified and lack uncertainty estimates.

relationships.condition: CIFAR-10 VGG, 90 epochs, augmentation and optimizer-specific learning-rate schedules
relationships.reason: R5–R7 show modest penalties: RMSProp 17.78% and Adam 18.02% versus SGD 17.32%, without uncertainty estimates.
relationships.display_finding: Reported modest error penalties for RMSProp and Adam relative to SGD remain unverified and lack uncertainty estimates.

relationships.condition: CIFAR-10 ResNet-20, 125 epochs, with optimizer-specific learning-rate schedules
relationships.reason: R9–R11 show small penalties of 0.49 and 0.43 percentage points; the stated fluctuation bound of 1% does not establish a reliable ordering.
relationships.display_finding: Reported small penalties remain unverified, and the stated fluctuation bound does not establish a reliable optimizer ranking.
